can_do_statement: Can invert the subject and affirmative auxiliary verb with 'hardly … when' to talk about something that happened immediately before something else, in formal contexts.
example_raw:
Hardly had she spoken these words when it dawned on the musician that life could not continue like that. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Spanish - European; Pass)

Hardly had he taken them from the counter when the monster vanished again. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 2000; Catalan; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: An action occurs immediately before another one.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'hardly had' adds formal emphasis to the speed of succession between events.

positives: Hardly had she spoken these words when it dawned on the musician.
Hardly had the teacher arrived when the bell rang.
negatives: She had hardly spoken when the bell rang.
Hardly anyone noticed when we left the party.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with an increasing range of verbs.
example_raw:
I forgot to tell you some details about tomorrow evening. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Turkish; Pass)

I spent about £35 on all those clothes. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

[talking about a football game] I liked it very much because my favourite team won, it was great. (Peru; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Action completed at a specific time in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple affirmative using regular or common irregular verbs.

positives: I forgot to tell you some details about tomorrow evening.
My favourite team won the championship.
negatives: I forget to tell you details.
My favourite team is winning.

can_do_statement: Can use 'yes/no' and 'wh-' question forms with 'you' with a limited range of verbs.
example_raw:
Did you buy something yesterday? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

[talking about a lost phone] Did you find it? (Albania; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Albanian; Pass)

And when did you go shopping last? (Russia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Russian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Seeking information about a completed past action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Forming questions in the past using 'did' with the pronoun 'you'.

positives: Did you buy something yesterday?
When did you quickly find it?
negatives: Do you buy something yesterday?
Have you found it yet?

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.
example_raw:
Every day at college I went to class at 9 am. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

I met her about ten years ago. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Others; Pass)

My grandmother lived in a village and I often went there. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Action completed at a specific time in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple affirmative using regular or irregular verbs.

positives: I went to class at 9 am.
My grandmother lived in a village.
negatives: I go to class at 9 am.
My grandmother lives in a village.

can_do_statement: Can use the past simple to talk about everyday events or states.
example_raw:
The people were very polite. (A1, French)

Every time I went to Hendon Park, I saw so many people there. (A1, Polish)

I liked this place very much. (A1, French)

ontology.mental_model: Everyday state or event completed in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using past simple for descriptions and recurring states.

positives: The people were very polite.
I liked this place very much.
negatives: The people are very polite.
I like this place very much.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.
example_raw:
The player from China did not look very happy though. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Chinese; Pass)

You did not keep your promise. (Bangladesh; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Bengali; Pass)

I didn't tell you that my house is opposite the new cinema. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - European; Pass)

They didn't cost much ... (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Panjabi; Pass)

I was surprised because the heating didn't work. (Poland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Polish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Stating that a past event did not happen.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'did not' or 'didn't' to form negative past statements.

positives: You did not keep your promise.
I didn't tell you that my house is opposite the cinema.
negatives: You do not keep your promise.
I haven't told you that my house is opposite.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with a wide range of verbs.
example_raw:
I convinced some of my friends to come with me even if they don't like rap music. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Italian; Pass)

Previously I faced many failures but I never gave up. (India; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Malayalam; Pass)

The cameraman filmed us during a lesson and later, walking to the playground. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Catalan; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Action completed at a specific time in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple affirmative applied to diverse verbs.

positives: I convinced some of my friends to come with me.
The cameraman suddenly filmed us during a lesson.
negatives: I convince some of my friends to come.
The cameraman is filming us.

can_do_statement: Can use 'when' + past simple in subordinate clauses.
example_raw:
When I arrived, the weather was horrible. (Argentina; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

[talking about a missing phone] I think I left it in the kitchen when I fell on the slippery floor. (Mexico; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Setting a point in time when something else happened.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'when' before a past simple clause.

positives: When I arrived, the weather was horrible.
I left it in the kitchen when I completely fell down.
negatives: When I arrive, the weather is horrible.
I am leaving it in the kitchen when I fall.

can_do_statement: Can use 'yes/no', 'wh-', tag and negative question forms with an increasing range of verbs.
example_raw:
Are you still looking for a job or did you succeed in finding one? (France; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)

When did you last see your wife and your children? (Germany; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; German; Pass)

It was great to have met you, and we certainly had a terrific time together, didn't we? (Portugal; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

Didn't you tell me that you had to go to Orleans today? (B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)

Why didn't you say something about it? (Argentina; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Seeking information about a completed past action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Questions in past simple using did or didn't.

positives: Did you succeed in finding one?
Didn't you completely tell me that?
negatives: Do you succeed in finding one?
Haven't you told me that?

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with an increasing range of verbs.
example_raw:
I didn't realise I had lost the ring till I was at home. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2000; Italian; Pass)

I didn't trust him. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Spanish - European; Pass)

[talking about a spare television] … we had one in the garage that we did not use. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Swedish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Stating that a past event did not happen.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'did not' or 'didn't' to form negative past statements.

positives: I didn't realise I had lost the ring.
We had one in the garage that we did not immediately use.
negatives: I don't realise I have lost the ring.
We have one in the garage that we do not use.

can_do_statement: Can use the past simple to talk about habitual states or actions.
example_raw:
… he always seemed so confident to me! (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Portuguese; Pass)

… we always talked during the class. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: A recurrent event or state in the past that is no longer happening.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple used with adverbs of frequency.

positives: He always seemed so confident to me.
We often talked during the class.
negatives: He always seems so confident to me.
We often talk during the class.

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect continuous to talk about repeated activities which began in the past and are still continuing.
example_raw:
I've been watching TV a lot, specially the sports programmes. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Portuguese; Pass) 

I have been playing my new game. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Turkish; Pass)

Last week I went out with my cousin Jim and his wife; he told me he had joined a sport club and he has been going there for two weeks; (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Italian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: An ongoing activity that started in the past and continues or has just finished.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present perfect continuous structure: have/has been + verb-ing.

positives: I've been watching TV a lot lately.
He has been going there for two weeks.
negatives: I am watching TV a lot.
He had been going there for two weeks.

example_raw:
I have been thinking about your letter. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

We've been studying together since grade one. (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

The letter was from my brother, who has been living in New York since he graduated from university. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Turkish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: An ongoing activity that started in the past and continues.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present perfect continuous structure: have/has been + verb-ing.

positives: We've been studying together since grade one.
I have recently been thinking about your letter.
negatives: We are studying together.
I had been thinking about your letter.

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect continuous with adverbs in the normal mid position.
example_raw:
I have just been reading an article in your newspaper this morning, about The Westfield Music Festival. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1997; Swedish; Pass)

I've also been singing in a choir for five years, so I'm very familiar with it. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Swedish; Pass)

You have already been complaining about headaches and insomia. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Polish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: An ongoing activity with emphasis via a mid-position adverb.

positives: I have just been reading an article.
You have already been complaining about headaches.
negatives: I just read an article.
You already complained about headaches.

can_do_statement: Can invert the subject and affirmative auxiliary verb with 'not only … but' as a focusing device. ► focus ► inversion
example_raw:
Not only have I been wandering its streets ever since I was ten, but I have also come to know most of the main characters of its history in the past 50 years. (Spain; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2000; Catalan; Pass)

Not only have I been expecting it for the last few months but I will also give some support to my wife, who has been feeling a little nervous these last weeks. (Portugal; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Focalizing two related ongoing activities by fronting 'not only'.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Inversion: 'Not only have I been...' to heighten emphasis.

positives: Not only have I been wandering its streets, but I also know the people.
Not only has she recently been studying hard, but she also works.
negatives: I have not only been wandering its streets.
Not only had I been wandering its streets.
